evidence: Single deployable unit (pybikes package) with 3 top-level packages (pybikes/, tests/, utils/)
Clear domain modularity: each system (e.g., aksu.py, bicing.py) implements a system-specific scraper deriving from common base classes (BikeShareSystem, BikeShareStation)
Shared core abstractions in pybikes/base.py (BikeShareSystem, BikeShareStation, Vehicle) and pybikes/gbfs.py (Gbfs base class)
Dependency hierarchy evident: individual systems inherit from base or GBFS, GBFS inherits from core base classes
No network/distributed communication patterns; all logic runs in-process
Repository depth of 3 layers (package/module/file) aligns with typical monolithic structure
Low average fan-out (2.45) suggests loose coupling within a bounded context
risks: Risk of tight coupling if shared utilities (e.g., utils.py) become god-objects
Potential performance issues as more systems are added without isolation
Test coverage may not scale if integration points are not well-defined
